properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised by Anthony asking how CI and regression testing here could be improved, 2026-09-21.

THE OBSERVATION, and it is arithmetic rather than opinion. The design models 7 budgets, 0 of them with a declared margin. The closure reading's budgets leg currently names one as exceeded — a read after a write was to cost at most twice the same read warm, and the rollup says 398. Whether that is a real 200x performance regression or stale contribution numbers is NOT DETERMINABLE FROM THE GRAPH, and this project has already recorded the failure in that exact shape: a perf fix updated the measured fact and never the CONSTRAINS edge, so the rollup reported "exceeded" for a budget that in fact held. A number that only a human refreshes will always eventually be a number nobody refreshed.

Half the instrument already exists. A detector names any limit whose check has no executable form, "until the file that is the check is linked" — so the design ALREADY ANTICIPATES an executable check per limit and is waiting for one. What is missing is the other half: a CI step that runs it and writes the number back. No performance gate of any kind runs in `ci.yml` today; the ~48 gates are all functional or structural.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) A BENCHMARK GATE for the limits that already exist — criterion or a plain timing harness for the handful of numeric constraints (graph construction under 1 ms, orientation under 8 s, loop_status after a write under a second), failing the build when the measured value exceeds the stated limit. The declared-margin hole matters here: with no margin, a gate is a cliff and will flap.
(b) MEASURE AND RECORD, NEVER FAIL — the same harness, but it only writes the measurement with its commit and date. The budget rollup then quotes a number the build took, and a person decides whether an exceeded budget stops anything. This is the option that is consistent with how this project treats drift everywhere else: report, and leave the disposition to the owner.
(c) RUN IT ONLY AT A RELEASE CUT, not on every push. CI runners are noisy and shared; per-push timing on a hosted runner is a well-known source of false red.
(d) NOTHING, and accept that budgets here are declarative intent rather than measured properties — which is honest, but then the budgets leg of the closure reading should say so rather than reporting a breach.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: timing on shared CI hardware is noisy enough that (a) buys a flapping gate, and a flapping gate is switched off. (b) and (c) are the versions that survive contact with a hosted runner.
properties.name: OPEN — should a modelled budget be a gate that MEASURES on every build, rather than a number somebody typed once and a rollup that may be quoting stale contributions?
properties.rationale: Recorded open because the choice is not really whether to measure but whether measuring is allowed to stop a build, and that turns on the missing declared margins rather than on the harness. Left unpromoted because option (d) — budgets are intent, not measurements — is a legitimate answer that would instead change what the closure reading claims.
